## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 00f9da2de0f662b4105b134e9f4c568c2a0e8e35

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation approach:** The fix commit `b53abc9a0` only touches the `onUpgrade()` switch statement in `KeychainDatabase.java`, renumbering every `case` label from `8…15` down to `7…14` and merging the content of the old `case 8` into `case 7`. Since `DATABASE_VERSION` stays `15` on both sides of the fix, this is purely a case-numbering consolidation. I used `git blame` on the pre-fix revision (`b53abc9a0^`) to attribute each `case` line to the commit that introduced it, then verified each of those commits individually with `git show`.

**(2) The specific defective change:** Before the fix, the chain looked like:
```
case 6:  ALTER TABLE ...                     (version bump 6→7, pre-existing, consistent)
case 7:  // consolidate   (empty)
case 8:  CREATE_API_APPS_ALLOWED_KEYS         <- single version bump 7→8, but TWO case labels added
case 9:  rename user_ids -> user_packets
...
case 15: ALTER TABLE ... name/email/comment
```
`git blame` shows `case 7` and `case 8` were both added in the *same* commit, `00f9da2de0f662b4105b134e9f4c568c2a0e8e35`, which also bumped `DATABASE_VERSION` from `7` to `8` — i.e. a single version increment, but it introduced two case labels (one empty "consolidate" placeholder plus the real migration). Up to that point the established invariant was "the highest `case` label equals `DATABASE_VERSION - 1`" (e.g. version 7 → last case is 6). This commit broke that invariant by shifting the real migration code one label too high (`case 8` instead of `case 7`).

Every later commit that bumped `DATABASE_VERSION` (`7f7da1471`, `c8dbe4dc6`, `75e47d487`, `3047cf3f7`, `010e58c8c`, `d5171750f`, `edf5de693`) each added exactly one new `case` matching the new version number, faithfully continuing the (already-wrong) pattern established by `00f9da2de0`. None of them introduced a new inconsistency — they just propagated the original one. `b53abc9a0` restores the original correct invariant by eliminating the superfluous `case 7` placeholder and shifting every subsequent case down by one.

**(3) Supporting evidence:**
- `git blame b53abc9a0^ -L 275,315 ...` shows `case 7` and `case 8` both attributed to `00f9da2de0`, the only point in the file's history where a single `DATABASE_VERSION` increment produced two new case labels.
- `git show 00f9da2de0 ...` confirms the diff: `DATABASE_VERSION 7→8`, plus addition of `case 7: // consolidate` immediately followed by `case 8: ... CREATE_API_APPS_ALLOWED_KEYS ...`.
- All subsequent version-bumping commits (`c8dbe4dc6`, `75e47d487`, `3047cf3f7`, `010e58c8c`, `d5171750f`, `edf5de693`) each add exactly one case per one version bump, matching the (off-by-one) convention set by `00f9da2de0` — they are mechanical continuations, not independent sources of the inconsistency.

**Uncertainty:** I traced the control flow carefully and could not find a case where the pre-fix numbering actually causes a *missed* migration step for any realistic upgrade path (the `switch`/fall-through dispatch still works correctly end-to-end because it matches on the real persisted `oldVersion` value, not on label-to-label relationships). So this appears to be primarily a consistency/maintainability fix (restoring the "`last case == DATABASE_VERSION - 1`" convention) rather than one that was causing an actively observable runtime failure at the time of the fix — though it is plausible it was proactively fixing a latent risk (e.g. to avoid a duplicate-case collision when the next version bump was added). I'm confident `00f9da2de0` is the commit that introduced the numbering irregularity the fix corrects; I'm less certain this irregularity itself produced a user-visible defect before being fixed.
